Good afternoon, Council.
The report before Council today is seeking direction around entering into a formal dispatch
service agreement with Waterloo Regional Police Services.
The City of Kitchener's bylaw enforcement team have relied on police dispatch services for 30 years.
Our bylaw staff work 24-7, 365 days a year and currently respond through police dispatch to noise complaints, fireworks, backyard fires and other enforcement type calls.
Until now, this service has been provided without a cost and without a formal agreement.
However, recent amendments to the Police Service Act now allow police service boards to recover costs for non-poor services, including dispatch services for municipal enforcement.
As a result, in late 2024, WRPS advised all area municipalities that they are moving to a formal region-wide dispatch model with cost recovery.
along with City of Kitchener, City of Waterloo, Cambridge, and the Township of North Dumfries
have opted to be part of the contract. The proposed model would provide dedicated bylaw-only
dispatchers, a separate radio channel, and a centralized phone number for bylaw calls.
The estimated annual cost to the City of Kitchener is approximately $587,000, which is based on call
volume and will be evaluated annually. The contract is slated to begin in July,
but WRPS will only begin to recover costs in October. Although the cost is significant,
staff evaluated alternative dispatch options, but these alternatives would result in comparable
costs while significantly reducing officer safety and response capabilities. By-law staff routinely
attend situations late at night that involve elevated risk, aggressive behavior, impaired
individuals or attend isolated locations. Continued access to police dispatch is vital
to keeping our staff safe as it allows for real-time safety information such as property
or person flags, police have the location of our officers and immediate support such
as going on police radio versus calling line 911 if police backup is needed.
The report before you outlines the service model, financial implications, and the rationale
for the recommendation of going with option one to remain with police dispatch through
a formal agreement.
